CHEMISTRY — MOCK EXAM #16
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: CHEMISTRY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

2. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

3. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Acids and Bases 2.2. Introduction to Salts 3.0 Organic Chemistry Page 15 of 40 1? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Acids and Bases 2.2. Introduction to Salts 3.0 Organic Chemistry Page 15 of 40 1.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Acids and Bases 2.2. Introduction to Salts 3.0 Organic Chemistry Page 15 of 40 1.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Acids and Bases 2.2. Introduction to Salts 3.0 Organic Chemistry Page 15 of 40 1.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Acids and Bases 2.2. Introduction to Salts 3.0 Organic Chemistry Page 15 of 40 1.

5. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. watt (W)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. joule (J)

6. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Removing all vegetation

7. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 100 °C

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Chemical Bonding ● valence electron in bonding ● bond type (ionic, covalent, dat? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Chemical Bonding ● valence electron in bonding ● bond type (ionic, covalent, dat.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Chemical Bonding ● valence electron in bonding ● bond type (ionic, covalent, dat.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Chemical Bonding ● valence electron in bonding ● bond type (ionic, covalent, dat.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Chemical Bonding ● valence electron in bonding ● bond type (ionic, covalent, dat.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Atom 1.3. The periodic Table 1.4. Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Phys? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on The Atom 1.3. The periodic Table 1.4. Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Phys.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Atom 1.3. The periodic Table 1.4. Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Phys.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Atom 1.3. The periodic Table 1.4. Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Phys.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Atom 1.3. The periodic Table 1.4. Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Phys.

10. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Only water vapour

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Acids and bases? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Acids and bases.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Acids and bases.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Acids and bases.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Acids and bases.

13. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

14. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Milk souring

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Atom? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Atom.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on The Atom.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Atom.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Atom.

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Periodicity ● Trends in groups I, II, VII, VIII and period 3 ● gradation in size? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Periodicity ● Trends in groups I, II, VII, VIII and period 3 ● gradation in size.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Periodicity ● Trends in groups I, II, VII, VIII and period 3 ● gradation in size.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Periodicity ● Trends in groups I, II, VII, VIII and period 3 ● gradation in size.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Periodicity ● Trends in groups I, II, VII, VIII and period 3 ● gradation in size.

17. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Periodic Table ● Development of the periodic table . ● Ion formation . ● For? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Periodic Table ● Development of the periodic table . ● Ion formation . ● For.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Periodic Table ● Development of the periodic table . ● Ion formation . ● For.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on The Periodic Table ● Development of the periodic table . ● Ion formation . ● For.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Periodic Table ● Development of the periodic table . ● Ion formation . ● For.

18. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water always increases oxygen

19. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Chemistry? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Chemistry.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Chemistry.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Chemistry.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Chemistry.

20. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2.? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2..
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2..
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2..
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2..

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. In three clear sentences, explain The Atom and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain The Periodic Table ● Development of the periodic table . ● Ion formation . ● For and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

27. In three clear sentences, explain Acids and bases and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

28. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
